instructions:
Below is an essay you revised once. Revise it so that it reads as if a US grade 11 student wrote it in class for a timed writing test. Keep the position it argues and keep it at about 475 words. The file must contain only the revised essay.

Essay:

In tenth grade my cousin broke her leg and she missed almost five weeks of school. Her teachers sent home packets of worksheets but nobody actually explained the chemistry to her. When she finally came back she was so far behind that she had to retake the whole class in summer school. If her school let her join class by video she probably would have only missed a couple days. That is the main reason why I think students should have the option to attend classes from home.

I want to be clear that I said option. I don't think every student should be on a laptop all year, because that would be bad for a lot of people. I just think the choice should be there for the kids who need it. Some students get sick for a long time or get hurt like my cousin did. Some live really far away and ride the bus for an hour each way, so that's two hours a day of basically doing nothing. There are also students who have really bad anxiety, and being in a crowded cafeteria makes it hard for them to focus on anything. For these students the choice isn't really between home and school. It's between learning at home and not learning.

Another reason is that learning from home lets students work in the way that is best for them. In a normal class the teacher explains it one time and then moves on to the next thing. A lot of online lessons are recorded, so if you didn't understand a math problem you can just watch it again and not have to act like you got it. Also some students have jobs after school to help their family, and they could do their work at night. It could help small schools too. A small school might not have a teacher for the third year of a language or for advanced physics, but students could take it online with a teacher from somewhere else.

Some people say that students at home will get distracted or lonely. I think they are kind of right. It is hard to pay attention when your bed and your phone are right next to you, and you can't really make friends through a screen. But this only proves online class is wrong for some students, not that nobody should be allowed to do it. Schools could take attendance, make students keep their cameras on in discussions, and require a certain grade to stay in the program. If a student starts failing then they have to come back to the building.

In conclusion, school is supposed to be about learning and not about what chair you are sitting in. Letting students attend from home would help more of them keep learning when something in their life goes wrong.
